newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech parliament board says backs securities watchdog.
newsitem.headline: Czech parliament board says backs securities watchdog.

text.p: The chairman of the Czech parliament's budget committee, which also watches over capital markets, said the committee had full support for an independent market watchdog like the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

"The commission for securities has 100 percent support of the budget committee and of informed members of the government (who know about its preparation)," budget committee chairman Josef Wagner said after a meeting with Prague Stock Exchange officials.

PSE Chairman Tomas Jezek, a former chairman of the same parliamentary committee, said that he and a working group were preparing legislation to set up the securities commission in order to start work next summer.
"We would like for the commission to start on the first of July next year," Jezek told the reporters at the same news conference with Wagner.
Czech analysts have long complained about insufficient oversight on the nascent markets where transparency of stock prices and the disclosure of investor and company information is often lacking.
Jezek, since becoming PSE chairman in April, has been repeatedly calling for an independent watchdog which would be financed through a fee charged on every transaction.
Jezek told reporters his plan would impose a fee of 0.02 percent on each trade, including off-market transactions registered at the Central Securities Registry (SCP).

To date, the government of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus have resisted any independent securities watchdog saying the problems on the capital markets were products of the transforming economy and would eventually vanish.
